rules.rule: If two paints are mixed to create a grey, they are mixing complements; visual complements (which produce afterimages) do not necessarily mix to grey.
rules.evidence: Mixing complements — two paints, dyes or inks that can be mixed in some proportion to make a grey.

rules.rule: If you stare at a saturated colour and look at a white surface, the ghost image appearing is the visual complement, which lies 180° opposite on the perceptual hue plane.
rules.evidence: Visual complements — two colours at opposite ends of a straight line drawn through the neutral centre of a perceptual hue plane. This is the pair your eye pairs, and the one the afterimage shows you.

rules.rule: If two colours have equal lightness, equal chroma, and a hard boundary between them, the viewer will perceive the edge as buzzing.
rules.evidence: If the pair sits at the same value and the same chroma with a hard edge between them, expect the boundary to buzz.

rules.rule: If you attempt to darken a colour by adding its visual complement, the mixture will lose chroma faster than it loses lightness and may not become neutral grey.
rules.evidence: Add the complement and you lose chroma faster than you lose lightness.
